title: Where is wisdom? (Job 28)
hookLine: miners dig out gold, "But wisdom, where shall it be found?"

lines: HANGING ON ROPES IN THE DARK.
cards: "Surely there is a vein for the silver, and a place for gold where they fine it." Chapter twenty-eight opens in a mine.
Someone cuts a shaft far from where people live and hangs on ropes, swinging, forgotten by anyone walking above.
They turn the mountains over by the roots, cut channels in the rock, find sapphires in the stones and dust of gold.
They go where no bird has gone: "There is a path which no fowl knoweth, and which the vulture's eye hath not seen." Down in the dark, they bring hidden things into the light.

teach.b: Almost. Then the turn: "But where shall wisdom be found? and where is the place of understanding?" We can dig to the roots of mountains, but nobody knows the way to that.

teach.h: THE DEPTH SAITH, IT IS NOT IN ME.
teach.b: "The depth saith, It is not in me: and the sea saith, It is not with me." Can you buy it?
The poem runs through the treasure room: gold, onyx, sapphire, coral, pearls, rubies, the topaz of Ethiopia. None of it is enough. Then where?

"God understandeth the way thereof, and he knoweth the place thereof." And the chapter ends with what God says to human beings: "Behold, the fear of the Lord, that is wisdom; and to depart from evil is understanding."

Notice where this poem sits. Job and his friends have argued chapter after chapter, the friends sure they know why Job suffers, Job sure they're wrong. Then this quiet poem drops in, like a pause in a shouting match.
Readers debate who is speaking: some hear Job, some hear the narrator stepping in. Either way, it tells everyone at the table: you can mine the earth, but you can't mine this.
Wisdom here isn't a pile of answers; the friends had answers. It's a way of standing, in awe of God and turned away from harm. It's what's left when the explanations run out.

how: Job 28 is studied in Jewish tradition as a poem on wisdom, and its closing line, the fear of the Lord is wisdom, echoes a teaching found also in Psalms and Proverbs.

o: a miner's song about finding gold in the dark
a poem saying only God knows the way to wisdom
a riddle Job's friends use to prove him guilty

games.q: where is wisdom — tap the pairs.
p: says it is not in me

s: Job 28 says wisdom can be bought if you have enough gold
gold, onyx, sapphire, coral, pearls, rubies: none of it is enough.
in the poem, the deep and the sea both say wisdom isn't in them
the depth saith, it is not in me; the sea saith, it is not with me.
everyone agrees Job is the one speaking in chapter 28
readers debate it: some hear Job, some the narrator.

games.q: you're a miner deep under the mountain. you've found silver, gold and sapphires. now you go looking for wisdom. where do you find it?
o: the poem says only God knows the way to it.
games.why: "God understandeth the way thereof." and to people he says: the fear of the Lord, that is wisdom; and to depart from evil is understanding.

practice: Bring to mind one question you've been digging at, why did this happen, what should I have done, and notice how hard you've been digging.

Then set the shovel down and ask a different question: how do I want to stand while I don't know, gently, honestly, turned away from harm? If you pray, you can bring the question to God and leave it there for now.

wordCard.voice: Where is wisdom? People can dig gold out of the dark, but the poem in Job twenty-eight says only God knows the way to wisdom. Today's word.

orig.note: Hebrew: wisdom; the word in the poem's question in Job 28:12.

carryVoice: Your line: where shall wisdom be found. Not in the mine, the poem says. That's day eight hundred forty-five.
